named.name: Makkedah
named.label: right
named.note: The campaign starts from Makkedah, taken the same day as the five kings were executed (v. 28).

named.name: Libnah
named.label: left
named.note: Its site is uncertain; Tel Burna (Tell Bornat) is OpenBible.info's leading suggestion, with Tel Goded and Tel Zayit also proposed.

named.name: Lachish
named.label: left
named.note: A large fortified city; it took a siege and fell on the second day (v. 32).

named.name: Gezer
named.label: right
named.note: Horam, king of Gezer, came to help Lachish and was defeated (v. 33). Gezer itself is not said to be captured; Josh 16:10 says it remained Canaanite.

named.name: Eglon
named.label: below
named.note: Tel Hesi is the main alternative site.

named.name: Hebron
named.label: right
named.note: "Went up" from Eglon (v. 36): Hebron lies high in the Judean hill country. Josh 14–15 and Judg 1 tell of Caleb taking Hebron again later.

named.name: Debir
named.label: below
named.note: Also called Kiriath-sepher (Josh 15:15). Khirbet Rabud is the leading identification; Tell Beit Mirsim is the older one.

moves.text: Horam king of Gezer comes to help Lachish
Joshua returns with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal

p: Verses 40–42 sum up the campaign: the hill country, the Negev, the Shephelah and the slopes, "from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, and the whole region of Goshen as far as Gibeon". Zoom out to see Kadesh-barnea and Gaza on the map. This Goshen is a district in the south of Judah, not the Goshen in Egypt.

The campaign is a series of raids that defeat kings and cities; later chapters show that several places still had to be taken again (Hebron and Debir in Josh 15:13–17 and Judg 1:10–15), and Gezer was never taken (Josh 16:10). Verse 43, like verse 15, returns Israel to Gilgal and is absent from the Greek Septuagint.
The order of the cities is the text's own. The lines between them are reconstructions drawn for teaching. Libnah and Eglon are probable rather than certain identifications.
